entry.title: [Soroushdabbagh_Official] The murmurings of 14. Sohrab in the notebook "The Traveler" and "The Green…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @Soroushdabbagh_Official

The murmurings of 14. Sohrab in the notebook "The Traveler" and "The Green Volume" was murmuring to himself: "The lover is always alone/ and the lover's hand is in the trembling hand of seconds/...He and the seconds sleep on light/ and he and the seconds give the best book in the world/ to the water/ and they know well/ that no fish ever/ untied the thousand and one knots of the river/ and at midnights with the old boat of illumination/ they set out on the waters of guidance/ and drive on until the manifestation of wonder." And: "Someone came and took my books/ drew a ceiling of the harmony of flowers over my head/ made my evening vast with repeated windows/ placed my table under the spirituality of rain." The contemplative Shirazi mystic also whispered to himself: "Seize the moment and drink in the rose garden, for the rose will not be there another week. Tear up the pages if you are my fellow student, for the knowledge of love is not in the notebook." And: "Speak of the minstrel and wine and seek less the secret of time, for no one has unraveled and no one will unravel this riddle through philosophy." And: "What is this tall ceiling, simple yet of many patterns? Of this riddle, no sage in the world is aware." What a strange creature the human being is! A two-legged migratory bird who passes night and day in this existence, estranged, in toil and turmoil. On one hand, he knows that acquiring knowledge and understanding is, in Aristotle's words, among the "virtues" that constitute the essence of your and my humanity; a knowledge found in books and notebooks that draws the wise in its wake. On the other hand, he sees wayfarers like Hafez and Sepehri, who were learned and erudite, at a stage of their existential journey laying down their shields, acknowledging the enigmatic and mysterious nature of existence, relinquishing the untying of knots, washing away the pages of lessons and exercises and notebooks and books and entrusting them to flowing water, placing "the burden of knowledge from the shoulders of the swallow onto the ground"; and they have tasted and savored a "transparent fear," a "wise silence," and a strange wonder and bewilderment that consumes the palate.

Quoted from the book: "Velvety Murmurings," Volume Two.
Author: Soroush Dabbagh

entry.title: [Soroushdabbagh_Official] "Every morning, a sorrow comes forth from the wheel of time." Upon hearing the…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @Soroushdabbagh_Official

"Every morning, a sorrow comes forth from the wheel of time." Upon hearing the news of the imprisonment of my dear friend and brother Dr. Mostafa Mehraeen to serve an eight-year sentence, I was truly grieved; just as I am bitterly saddened for other political prisoners, and I pray from the bottom of my heart for the freedom of each and every one of them. Mehraeen, in the role of a knowledgeable and compassionate sociologist, has earnestly, courageously, and honestly expressed his frank and unvarnished criticisms of the ineffective style of governance in the country through his pen and his loud voice, like my dear Mostafa Tajzadeh. No matter how much I think, the issuance of harsh and severe sentences and the imprisonment of these elites carries no weight on the scales of justice and fairness, and is truly an oppressive act... For more than three decades, I have sat at the table of the wisdom and literature of Hafez Shirazi and have learned from him as much as I could. A few days ago, it was the twentieth of Mehr, coinciding with the commemoration day of this genius of Shiraz; the rogue of stoic thought who, in his elegant ghazals, in addition to addressing philosophical and existential matters, had a critical eye on the record of the ascetics, preachers, jurists, and Sufis of his time, and by observing what was happening around him, would cry out in pain: They count hypocrisy as lawful and the cup of wine as forbidden — what a path and creed, what a sharia and faith. And: They closed the door of the tavern, O God, do not allow that they open the door of the house of hypocrisy and pretense. And: Drink wine, for a hundred sins concealed by others are better than a devotion performed with pretense and hypocrisy. Sadly, we live in circumstances where the Minister of Education insists on "compulsory prayer," and after several years since the blessed movement "Woman, Life, Freedom," "unveiling" is criminalized; measures from which the smell of coercion and hypocrisy is clearly sensed. At the same time, in addition to insisting on carrying out executions whose cases, by the testimony of experts, lacked proper and defensible due process; intellectuals and political activists who radiate liberty, honesty, and courage from head to toe taste the flavor of imprisonment, torment, and prison. It is clear in such a sorrowful and dust-covered situation, on which pivot the wheel turns and to what extent governance has strayed from the orbit of fairness, justice, and effectiveness, and how much has been added to the volume of citizens' suffering... https://www.instagram.com/p/DecUHUpxz-N/?obrf=MXhmdzhrMjcyNWdiNA==
